annotation:
Both "Arnold Layne" and "Candy and a Currant Bun" were mixed into mono for the single. Neither have ever been given a stereo mix, although the four-track master tapes still exist in the EMI tape archive

Recorded over two sessions at different studios:
1967-01-29 at Sound Techniques Studios, London, UK
1967-02-27 at EMI Studios, London, UK

title: Bomb Intro / Pass That Dutch
annotation:
This is the original recording, the Bomb Intro is a spoken-word piece by Missy that starts ""Listen up, everyone/We have been just informed ...".

A version that is around 3.42 in length also exists on many releases, and is sonically the same as this original album version with a slightly extended instrumental outro.

My English teacher wanted to '''flunk me''' in junior high
'''Thanks a lot, next semester I'll be 35'''
I smacked him in his face with an eraser, chased him with a stapler
'''And stapled his nuts to a stack of paper'''

annotation:
'''This recording should be kept as ''"Thankyou"''.''' Hit ''Show more'' below for evidence of its use in Dido's releases, and etymology of the word.

== "Thankyou" or "Thank You" ==
This recording is primarily called “'''''Thankyou'''''” as one word across 14 years of Dido releases:
    * on the original releases of '''''No Angel''''' in '''1999''' (for example, the [https://musicbrainz.org/release/7a9b4a0c-0888-4889-804b-eae4f6a2d4b5|US CD])
    * on subsequent re-releases of '''''No Angel''''' (for example, '''2003''''s [https://musicbrainz.org/release/798d5391-14e6-3347-88ce-6d43f7e3b86a|vinyl reissue] or '''2008''''s [https://musicbrainz.org/release/19a11727-e7b3-4eb8-ad3f-67e5e458c725|CD digipak reissue])
    * on the '''2005''' [https://musicbrainz.org/release/9dc4efb5-addd-4d65-81ed-abfd27edfbb1|Live at Brixton Academy DVD/CD release] (both UK and US versions)
    * the '''2013''' [https://musicbrainz.org/release/8a729d64-0d1d-44d1-ac37-faa6c4e5ac06|Greatest Hits] compilation
    * the only notable exception is the '''2001''' [https://musicbrainz.org/release/4b35b1bb-0a54-4f72-9327-3929aa5bcbbb|single release] which consistently uses "thank you"

Please leave this recording, and the tracklistings for Dido albums, as printed on the package, as this is clearly an official title used by Dido and/or the production company of her albums.

Various Artists releases, and streaming releases, often have it as “'''''Thank You'''''”. In those cases, it can be entered to the release as written.

----
== "Thankyou" isn't a word ==
Yes, it is, in British English at least where Dido is from (and perhaps other variants of English too). It is slightly different to "thank you". I would '''thank you''' for doing something, or I could give you a '''thankyou''' gift for doing something. For a fuller explanation: https://www.future-perfect.co.uk/grammar-tips/easy-mistakes/is-it-thank-you-thankyou-or-thank-you

Within the lyrics themselves, the grammar calls for the two-word version, but that isn't really relevant. Titles and lyrics often don't match up, and titles of things often aren't grammatically correct due to being a few words long, or sentence snippets.

Bing Crosby re-recorded White Christmas on March 19, 1947, accompanied again by the Trotter Orchestra and the Darby Singers, with every effort made to reproduce the original recording session The re-recording is recognizable by the addition of flutes and celesta in the beginning.
